summary: Established a robust architectural governance framework integrating AST-based parsing, deterministic model pinning, and an Idempotent Execution Guard, while evolving the knowledge management system into a Bloom-Adaptive Active Recall engine using DSR-based Spaced Repetition. Implemented systemic feedback loops, including 'LLM-as-a-Judge' gates and data sanitization filters, to ensure architectural output quality, prevent model divergence, and prioritize high-friction retrieval practice over passive logging.
key_learnings: AST-based parsing and model pinning ensure system determinism, while DSR-based SRS models provide superior scalability for memory management.
Active recall categorized by cognitive depth is more effective than keyword-based retrieval.
Systemic feedback loops and data sanitization are critical to mitigate bias, prevent divergence, and ensure high-fidelity knowledge synthesis.
Architectural decisions must prioritize hot-path efficiency and schema versioning to maintain long-term system stability.
